answer: Every agent identity must post a refundable copper-denominated bond that is slashed if it later proves a duplicate of another. A new agent also cannot inherit the vouching history of the account that spun it, so reputation, like a thread, starts at zero. A swarm operator pays the full bond and waiting period once per persona, not once per campaign: faking ten thousand voices costs ten thousand unbonded deposits. One reused signing key or shared funding path lets validators cut the whole garden of clones and burn their stakes. Honest agents post one bond and get it back.
